title: Visual Quickstart: Dedicated Capacity Flow & SLA Cards
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Goal: Produce a set of high-fidelity UX assets and annotated screenshots for the Dedicated onboarding quickstart that cover: capacity setup, autoscaling policy creation, and SLA overview. These assets will be used in the product Quickstart flow, in the Docs (Quickstart guide), and in the Release notes visuals for console-2026.03.

Scope of deliverables:
- 6 high-fidelity screens (desktop):
  1) Capacity selector: single-page view with recommended capacity presets (Dev / Prod / Custom), cost estimate strip, and recommended GPU types.
  2) Capacity details modal: advanced view showing vCPU/GPU equivalence, concurrency slider, token throughput preview.
  3) Autoscaling policy editor: form with Min / Target / Max instances, warm pool toggle, target latency (ms) or utilization %, preview graph.
  4) Autoscaling confirmation flow: success state + rollout notes and rollback button.
  5) SLA overview card: summary card showing Availability (99.9%), p50/p95 token latencies, escalation contacts, and included runbook link.
  6) Error / insufficient quota state: illustration + CTA to request capacity or contact Sales.

Acceptance criteria (must be met before marking Done):
- Screens match Redwood visual system tokens (colors, spacing, icons) and responsive grid rules.
- All interactive elements annotated (hover states, keyboard focus, aria labels).
- Microcopy copy-ed with PM-approved phrasing (see link to Confluence below).
- Exported PNGs at 2x and SVGs for illustrations; source Figma components shared with Engineering and Docs.
- Accessibility checks: contrast ratio >= 4.5:1 for primary text, controls reachable by keyboard, and at least one text alternative for visuals.
- Design handoff notes include prop names, behavior for edge cases (zero capacity, scaling failure), and suggested telemetry hooks (events to track).

Design constraints & trade-offs:
- Goal is clarity for first-time Dedicated customers; we prioritize a simplified capacity slider + preset options over exposing every hardware permutation. Engineering will receive a detailed advanced modal for power users.
- Autoscaling graph is illustrative (projected) not real-time; copy must indicate it shows expected behavior rather than SLA guarantees.

Handoff artifacts and links:
- Figma file (workboard): https://www.figma.com/file/Redwood/Dedicated-Onboarding-Quickstart (designers: please use frames named DES-4021-*)
- Confluence PRD / microcopy: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRD/pages/DED-Quickstart-Microcopy
- Example screenshots to capture from staging: https://staging.console.redwood.com/dedicated/quickstart
- Example GH issue for engineering work: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/issues/4221

Engineering notes (for compatibility):
- Autoscaling UI must map to API fields: min_instances, target_util_pct, max_instances, warm_pool_enabled. Confirm types with ENG-2108.
- Capacity estimator needs a simple client-side cost calc: tokens/sec * model_cost_per_token + GPU-hour estimate. Wireframe provided.
- Rollback CTA should trigger the existing rollout workflow; tie to ENG-2144.

Deliverable timeline:
- 2026-03-16: first-pass frames in Figma (ready for PM review)
- 2026-03-18: incorporate PM/Eng feedback and produce annotated handoff
- 2026-03-24: final assets delivered (PNG@2x + source frames + spec doc)

Acceptance sign-off: PM (Jordan Reyes), Eng lead (Priya Nair), Design lead (Diego Morales).
